llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Cue fact-checking integration, but it should be reviewed because it installs and updates an external runner and sends user material to Cue with shareable report links by default.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses git, python3, curl, a Cue API key from ~/.cue/config.json or CUE_API_KEY, network access to cuecue.cn, and local output under ~/cue-reports; these are broadly proportionate but require user awareness.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First use clones or fast-forwards an external GitHub/Gitee repository into ~/.cue/cue-skills and then runs a Python script from it, without pinning a commit, checksum, or reviewed release.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are mostly task-focused, but they require report-link delivery by default and include active referral/recharge guidance on insufficient credits, which goes beyond neutral fact-checking execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists the runner and report files in the user's home directory but does not define background services, hooks, or scheduled tasks; sudo appears only as optional Ubuntu package installation guidance for document conversion.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated fact-checking purpose matches the Cue API workflow, but user-submitted content is sent to cuecue.cn and the skill requires a shareable report URL by default, which can matter for sensitive documents or allegations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending the fact-check material to cuecue.cn and receiving a shareable report link. Review or pin the external cue-skills runner before use, keep the Cue API key scoped and protected, and avoid optional sudo package installs unless you explicitly need Word/PDF conversion.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: The cited curl commands fetch Cue health/playbook API JSON and pipe JSON to local Python; that specific evidence does not show remote code execution. The separate unpinned runner clone/update is the real supply-chain concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The artifact is Chinese-first throughout. That is a locale/usability limitation rather than a standalone security concern in this review.
[SDI-1] expected: A local runner supports the stated workflow, but cloning/updating mutable third-party code and executing it expands the trust boundary beyond the reviewed skill package.
[PE2] expected: The sudo references are optional apt install examples for pandoc/LaTeX conversion, not part of the main fact-check runtime.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote submission and share-link output are core to the Cue workflow and are partly disclosed, but the artifact lacks a clear pre-upload warning and makes link delivery mandatory unless the user opts out.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The referral and recharge instructions are not needed to perform fact-checking and could steer the agent into promotional guidance when credits are insufficient.
